post.title: Why Picking Your Own Lottery Numbers Feels Luckier #shorts
post.description: What's your lucky thing? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend with the lucky socks. Lila won't take a random ticket in the office lottery: she picks her own numbers. In 'The Illusion of Control' (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1975), Ellen Langer sold $1 lottery tickets to office workers. Some chose their own ticket, others were simply handed one. When asked to sell it back, people who had chosen their ticket asked for $8.67 on average, against $1.96 for people who were handed one, even though every ticket had exactly the same odds. Choosing feels like control, even when it changes nothing. #psychology #shorts #illusionofcontrol #luck #overthinking
